channel.title: Our State Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Our State Magazine (ourstate.com)

item.title: Community Blooms in Fremont
item.description: In this Wayne County town, residents don yellow and green to celebrate the flower that put them on the map.

item.title: Where Her Work Still Speaks
item.description: From a reclaimed community center to a long-forgotten cemetery, the Cumberland County land Ammie Jenkins tended keeps telling her story.

item.title: Signs of Care
item.description: The names on Adopt-A-Highway placards belong to neighbors who show up, suit up, and help keep North Carolina beautiful.

item.title: Charlie’s Soaps: A Laundry Legend
item.description: What began as a fix for gummed-up textile machines has grown into a family-run company with a devoted following, still made in the same quiet corner of Rockingham County.

item.title: A River Made New
item.description: After decades of pollution brought an Onslow County waterway to the brink, citizens, scientists, and Jacksonville city leaders worked together to restore their river.

item.title: Tending the Quiet Corners of the Coast
item.description: In hidden cemeteries from Buxton to Avon, Dawn Taylor cleans and restores weathered gravestones, ensuring that the lives they mark are not lost to the wind or the water.

item.title: Breathing Room in Stoneville
item.description: At a Rockingham County retreat center, stillness opens the door for clarity and renewal.

item.title: Waiting in the Rafters
item.description: Our State’s managing editor and her husband discover an attic room filled with pottery, hidden treasures that had been waiting overhead for decades.

item.title: Confessions of a Pack Rat
item.description: In the sandy shells, worn ticket stubs, and chipped mugs he can’t seem to part with, a sentimental saver finds a map to memories and meaning.

item.title: Porch Perfect
item.description: March in North Carolina is a fickle thing, but a writer in Greensboro takes advantage of the first warm days to scrub his porch and roll out the red carpet for spring.
